tools.name: trader_login
tools.description: Use this when you need to sign in before calling a tool that takes an auth_token and MT_AUTH_TOKEN is not set. Returns a link to verify your X identity and the command that saves the session token, which stays valid for 30 days.

tools.name: trader_my_stats
tools.description: Use this for a quick snapshot of your own standing: composite score, rank, total trades, qualified status and open positions (free, own account only). For returns, drawdown and win rate use trader_performance_report; for other traders use trader_search_trader.

tools.name: trader_performance_report
tools.description: Use this when you want a detailed breakdown of your own results over a timeframe: return statistics, volatility, Sharpe ratio, maximum drawdown, win rate, composite score and the scoring weights. For a quick score and rank check use trader_my_stats.

tools.name: trader_last_trade
tools.description: Use this when you want to see a trader's most recent trade (action, symbol, quantity, price, time) and their total trade count; free, no auth_token, works for any trader. It returns one trade only, so for a list of trades use trader_get_trade_history.

tools.name: trader_cancel_last
tools.description: Use this when you made a mistake and want to undo your most recent trade; it deletes the trade and updates your position, but only within 5 minutes of it being made, and the deletion cannot be undone. Acts only on your own account.

tools.name: trader_watch
tools.description: Use this when you want to add a trader to your watchlist; returns your updated watch count (activity notifications are not available yet). You must have made a trade yourself and cannot watch yourself; to remove a trader use trader_unwatch.

tools.name: trader_unwatch
tools.description: Use this when you want to remove a trader from your watchlist; returns a confirmation and is safe to repeat. To add a trader use trader_watch.

tools.name: trader_get_leaderboard
tools.description: Use this when you want the ranked list of top traders for a timeframe; paid with x402 ($0.25 USDC on Base for up to 100 rows, plus $0.01 per 4 more rows, maximum 500; call without payment to see the exact price). To look up one trader use trader_search_trader or trader_last_trade.

tools.name: trader_search_trader
tools.description: Use this when you want to find a trader by X handle or display name; returns up to 50 matches with handle, name, score, rank, trade count and qualified status. Paid with x402 ($0.02 USDC on Base; call without payment first to get the requirements). For the full ranking use trader_get_leaderboard.

tools.name: trader_get_trade_history
tools.description: Use this when you want a trader's list of trades, newest first (action, symbol, asset class, quantity, price, time); free for your own trades with auth_token, otherwise $0.01 USDC per 3 trades with x402 on Base (call without payment to see the price). For only the latest trade use trader_last_trade.

findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "trader_login" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

evidence.snippet: Use this when you need to sign in before calling a tool that takes an auth_token and MT_AUTH_TOKEN is not set. Returns a link to verify your X identity and the …

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "trader_login" references sensitive artifacts (session token). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "trader_login" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
